newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Business as usual despite Zimbabwe strike call.
newsitem.headline: Business as usual despite Zimbabwe strike call.

text.p: Zimbabweans on Wednesday for the second day running ignored calls by trade unions for a nationwide strike to press the government to resolve a crippling three-week stoppage by state nurses and doctors.

A chief executive at an industrial firm in Harare said all his workers turned up, adding that he sympathised with the Zimbabwe Congress of Trade Unions' (ZCTU) calls for action on the public health crisis but did not support industrial action.

"I don't go along with their calls for a strike, selfishly, because then business suffers. I think the government must sit down with the nurses and doctors and resolve this crisis because the situation is terrible," he told Reuters, requesting anonymity.
Two of the country's major hospitals -- Parirenyatwa and Harare -- have been closed by the strike.
ZCTU leaders -- who called for a two-day general strike after riot police used teargas and batons to stop their protest march on Monday -- were unavailable for comment.

Despite growing public pressure, the government of President Robert Mugabe has refused to negotiate with the nurses, who went on strike on October 21 and were joined last week by doctors to demand higher pay and improved working conditions.
It accuses its opponents, who deny the charges, of using the strikers to undermine its authority.

Early on Wednesday, scores of riot police patrolled a central Harare park which has been a rallying point for protesters but they were withdrawn from major buildings where they were deployed on Monday in a move a government minister said was aimed at protecting workers from being intimidated into joining the strike.
